original_wisa_caption:
The video begins with a first-person perspective of someone sliding down a water slide inside an aquarium. The person is wearing black flip-flops and is lying on their back, with their legs extended forward. The slide is enclosed by glass walls, through which various fish can be seen swimming. As the person slides down, the camera captures the movement of the water and the fish, creating a dynamic and immersive experience. The water appears clear, allowing for a good view of the fish and the slide's interior.

As the person continues to slide, the camera angle shifts slightly, providing a closer look at the fish swimming near the glass walls. The fish are of different sizes and colors, adding to the visual interest. The camera then pans upwards, revealing more of the aquarium's interior, including additional fish and possibly other aquatic life. The lighting in the aquarium is bright, enhancing the visibility of the fish and the details of the environment.

caption: A first-person view from a rider on a mat carries forward through an enclosed water-slide flume. The left side is a curved transparent wall streaked with rainbow-colored light refractions, through which a dim external structure is faintly discernible, while the right side opens into a rippling water channel. A rider's hand grips a looped yellow handle at the bottom of the frame, and far ahead a rectangular tunnel portal glows orange with a second rider visible inside it. The point of view drifts leftward as the rider advances. As the flume carries on, the orange portal and the distant rider slide steadily toward the right edge and leave the frame, so the caustic-covered wall claims an ever larger share of the image. A pale elongated silhouette emerges on the left portion of the wall. The hand and yellow handle shift toward the lower-right corner and leave the frame. The water ripples continuously, and the diagonal line where wall meets ceiling climbs upward across the top of the frame. The forward drift and leftward pan of the view continue without resolution.

claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
